item.title: Switch 1 & 2 Cartridges Under Threat As Key ROM Manufacturer Exits Business

description.p: Move may accelerate transition to digital.Macronix, one of Nintendo's key ROM manufacturers for physical game cartridges, is ceasing the production of ROM altogether.This comes via analyst David Gibson who relayed the news from Macronix's latest financial release. According to the data, ROM products accounted for just 5% of the firm's overall revenue for Q3 2026, representing a stark decrease of 39% year-on-year.Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Nintendo Joins The Accessible Games Initiative, Adopting A Bunch Of New eShop Game Tags

description.p: Tag, you're it!Nintendo has joined the Accessible Games Initiative and, in the process, has added a collection of new accessibility tags to the eShop.The new tags — which include various accessibility features like 'Narrated Menus', 'Full Input Remapping', and 'Playable with Buttons Only' — make it easier to sort through games based on specific requirements. Simply select a tag from the eShop Tags page, and it will bring up every game where that requirement can be applied.Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: The First Review For Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Switch 2 Is In

description.p: Famitsu delivers its final verdict.It's a huge week in gaming with the highly anticipated launch of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Switch 2. The first review from the famous Japanese outlet Famitsu has now officially gone live. So, what did it think of Nintendo's remake?If you aren't familiar with this publication's unique scoring system, four critics each deliver a score out of ten, and these scores are then totalled. For Ocarina of Time on the Switch 2, it's received 9/9/9/10, giving it an overall score of 37/40. So, it's been well received by the outlet!Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: "I Had Some Overdue Homework" - Ocarina Of Time Remake Features More Water Temple Tweaks

description.p: Yes, Aonuma knows how much you hate those Iron Boots.It's no secret that Eiji Aonuma can see the issues with Ocarina of Time's Water Temple. The series producer spoke about it when the game launched on 3DS, and it continues to haunt him today, as he's brought it up once again in the latest Ask the Developer interview."I had some overdue homework: I wanted to do something about the Water Temple I created 28 years ago," Aonuma-san says of the Switch 2 remake. He touches on all the dungeon's much-discussed sticking points (the item menu annoyances, confusing layout, etc.), and confirms that he "had the team make some adjustments in this version".Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Cosy Witch RPG 'Witchbrook' Will Support Crossplay Between Switch 1 & 2 At Launch

description.p: Switchbrook.It has been a good couple of weeks for Witchbrook news. After keeping an eye on Chucklefish's witch RPG for years, we finally got a release date in last month's Indie World Showcase (28th January, for those wondering), and now the developer has confirmed that Switch 1 & 2 players will be able to play with each other at launch.As highlighted by Smash Jump, one of the game's developers took to the Witchbrook Discord channel late last month to announce that Switch 1-to-2 crossplay would not be available at launch, but would be added down the line. Things changed in the ensuing week, it seems, as the dev later followed up the message with the following correction: "Update: Switch 1 and 2 will be able to play together".Read the full article on nintendolife.com
